question: In pure clostridial gas gangrene, the Gram stain of infected tissue characteristically shows abundant polymorphonuclear leucocytes surrounding the Gram-positive rods.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. A pathognomonic feature of pure clostridial gas gangrene is the ABSENCE of PMNs — alpha toxin lyses leucocytes immediately upon arrival. This distinguishes it from mixed necrotising infections where PMNs are abundant. Remember: rods WITHOUT pus cells = Clostridium; rods WITH pus cells = mixed infection.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! The hallmark of pure clostridial gas gangrene is Gram-positive rods in the ABSENCE of PMNs — alpha toxin destroys leucocytes as fast as they arrive. If you see pus (abundant PMNs) WITH gas, suspect a polymicrobial type I necrotising fasciitis rather than pure clostridial myonecrosis.
